A39953D0DFE601314B6A68A86D17958E.description: Identify similarities and differences between dramatic characters and real people.

A39889C0DFE601314B6868A86D17958E.description: Students recognize and explain how theatrical experiences contribute to a better understanding of history, culture, and human relationships.

A3984F40DFE601314B6768A86D17958E.description: Identify the differences between fantasy and reality.

A397D6F0DFE601314B6568A86D17958E.description: Express personal reactions to a dramatized performance.

A3975790DFE601314B6368A86D17958E.description: Students apply and demonstrate critical and creative thinking skills in theater, film television, or electronic media.

A3970F40DFE601314B6268A86D17958E.description: Use voice and body to show different emotions while portraying a character in a dramatized idea or story.

A3969470DFE601314B6068A86D17958E.description: Imitate the traits of a given person, animal, or object.

A3961570DFE601314B5E68A86D17958E.description: Identify traits of a person, animal, or object (e.g. What does a dog do when it's happy? Wag its tail).

A3959170DFE601314B5C68A86D17958E.description: Students understand and demonstrate the role of the actor in the theater.

A3953800DFE601314B5B68A86D17958E.description: Assemble and use simple props, costumes, masks, or make-up for a dramatized idea or story.

A394BA40DFE601314B5968A86D17958E.description: Create simple sets and sound effects for a dramatized idea or story (e.g. tables become caves).

A3943710DFE601314B5768A86D17958E.description: Create a simple script based on personal experience, imagination, or the retelling of a story.

A393AB50DFE601314B5568A86D17958E.description: Students recognize the components of theatrical production including script writing, directing, and production.

document.title: Nevada Social Studies Standards

A51CFBC0DFE601314DE968A86D17958E.description: Identify their city, state, and country.

A51C7200DFE601314DE768A86D17958E.description: Global Relations - Students explain the different political systems in the world and how those systems relate to the United States and its citizens.

A51C2680DFE601314DE668A86D17958E.description: Introduce sources of information people use to form an opinion.

A51B3490DFE601314DE368A86D17958E.description: List the qualities of a leader.

A51AA840DFE601314DE168A86D17958E.description: The Political Process - Students describe the roles of political parties, elections, interest groups, media, and public opinion in the democratic process.

A51A60F0DFE601314DE068A86D17958E.description: Name the current mayor of the town.

A51A08D0DFE601314DDF68A86D17958E.description: Name the current President of the United States.

A5198000DFE601314DDD68A86D17958E.description: The Federal System: U.S., State, and Local Governments - Students understand the U.S. Constitution and the government it creates, including the relationship between national and sub-national governments, as well as the structure and function of state and local governments.

A5193DF0DFE601314DDC68A86D17958E.description: Explain why we have patriotic activities, holidays, and symbols.

A518FB00DFE601314DDB68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the Pledge of Allegiance and discuss its purpose.

A5186860DFE601314DD968A86D17958E.description: Explain individual responsibilities in the classroom and the school.

A517D390DFE601314DD768A86D17958E.description: Discuss that democracy involves voting, majority rule, and setting rules.

A51748E0DFE601314DD568A86D17958E.description: Identify and discuss examples of rules, laws, and authorities that keep people safe and property secure.

A516A450DFE601314DD368A86D17958E.description: Citizenship and the Law - Students know why society needs rules, laws, and government and understand the roles, rights, and responsibilities of citizens.

A521AEF0DFE601314DF868A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between barter and monetary trade.

A520E3D0DFE601314DF668A86D17958E.description: The International Economy - Students will explore trends in international trade, the impact of trade on the U.S. economy, and the role of exchange rates.

A5209D60DFE601314DF568A86D17958E.description: Identify classroom resources that are limited and must be shared.

A5200FB0DFE601314DF368A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain what business owners do.

A51F6A50DFE601314DF168A86D17958E.description: The Dynamic Economy - Students will identify the causes of economic change; explain how the U.S. economic system responds to those changes; and explain how other economic systems respond to change.

A51E7180DFE601314DEE68A86D17958E.description: Define banking terms, including saving, interest, and borrowing.

A51DD530DFE601314DEC68A86D17958E.description: Identify forms of money used by people across time and place.

A51D3F60DFE601314DEA68A86D17958E.description: The U.S. Economy as a Whole - Students will identify indicators used to measure economic performance, understand key aspects of how the economy acts as a system, and understand the roles of money, interest rates, savers, and borrowers, financial institutions, and the central bank in our economy.

A5248550DFE601314E0168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an understanding of income and give examples.

A523D210DFE601314DFF68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of prices set by businesses for selling goods and services.

A52341D0DFE601314DFD68A86D17958E.description: Give examples of prices consumers have paid when buying goods and services.

A522A8E0DFE601314DFB68A86D17958E.description: Identify needs as high priority wants, and wants as goods, services, or leisure activities.

A5221010DFE601314DF968A86D17958E.description: The Market Economy - Students will understand how scarcity and incentives affect choices, how markets work, why markets form, how supply and demand interact to determine the market price, and how changes in prices act as economic signals to coordinate trade.

A532DD00DFE601314E2E68A86D17958E.description: Describe ways humans depend on and manage natural resources within their communities.

A53227C0DFE601314E2C68A86D17958E.description: Identify people, groups, and organizations that respond to natural hazards.

A531DF30DFE601314E2B68A86D17958E.description: Effects of Natural Hazards on Human Systems

A5318FE0DFE601314E2A68A86D17958E.description: Compare ways people modify the physical environment.

A5313F20DFE601314E2968A86D17958E.description: List tools, machines, or technologies that people have used to change the physical environment.

A530EC60DFE601314E2868A86D17958E.description: Technology & Modifications of the Physical Environment

A530A9E0DFE601314E2768A86D17958E.description: Predict possible geographic changes that could take place in the neighborhood or community.

A53021A0DFE601314E2568A86D17958E.description: Environment and Society - Students understand effects of interactions between human and physical systems and the changes in use, distribution, and importance of resources.

A52F3700DFE601314E2268A86D17958E.description: Use a map to display information about an economic product.

A52E9AB0DFE601314E2068A86D17958E.description: List reasons why people choose to live in urban or rural communities.

A52D4870DFE601314E1C68A86D17958E.description: Compare population distribution across regions using maps and mathematical representations, i.e., tables and graphs.

A52C8260DFE601314E1A68A86D17958E.description: Human Systems - Students understand how economic, political, and cultural processes interact to shape patterns of human migration and settlement, influence and interdependence, and conflict and cooperation.

A52C3960DFE601314E1968A86D17958E.description: Identify latitude and longitude on a map or globe.

A52BED60DFE601314E1868A86D17958E.description: Locate and name the states surrounding Nevada.

A52B53A0DFE601314E1668A86D17958E.description: List ways people use technology for geographic purposes, i.e., weather forecasting, use of aerial photographs to measure population changes over time.

A52B0F00DFE601314E1568A86D17958E.description: Patterns of Change & Impact of Technology

A52AC5E0DFE601314E1468A86D17958E.description: List ways people view their own communities, i.e., a ranching community, a tourist destination.

A529DB40DFE601314E1168A86D17958E.description: Identify characteristics of neighborhoods and communities, i.e., physical geographical differences, land use, population density.

A5298700DFE601314E1068A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between physical (natural) and human (man-made) features.

A5293990DFE601314E0F68A86D17958E.description: Application of Concepts & Characteristics of Places & Regions

A528E5E0DFE601314E0E68A86D17958E.description: Places & Regions - Students understand the physical and human features of places and use this information to define and study regions and their patterns of change.

A5289BB0DFE601314E0D68A86D17958E.description: List careers requiring the use of geographic tools.

A5285010DFE601314E0C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize different types of special maps, i.e., neighborhood, school, and classroom.

A527A980DFE601314E0A68A86D17958E.description: Construct a simple map including a title, symbols, and directions from a bird's eye view.

A526E0D0DFE601314E0868A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain simple spatial patterns on a map, i.e., population centers, farmland, mountains.

A5269020DFE601314E0768A86D17958E.description: Compare uses of maps and globes.

A525E160DFE601314E0568A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between a city and a state using appropriate examples.

A5257EA0DFE601314E0468A86D17958E.description: Identify and use cardinal directions on a compass rose to locate places on a map.

A524EAD0DFE601314E0268A86D17958E.description: The World in Spatial Terms: Students use maps, globes, and other geographic tools and technologies to locate and extrapolate information about people, places, and environments.

A538BB50DFE601314E4168A86D17958E.description: Discuss the effects of news events on people in the community.

A537FBC0DFE601314E3F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how technology at home and in school impacts their lives.

A537B2F0DFE601314E3E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate respect for each other, the community, and the world.

A5376ED0DFE601314E3D68A86D17958E.description: Define ethnicity and explain that people who make contributions to their communities include those who have diverse ethnic origins, customs, and traditions.

A5372900DFE601314E3C68A86D17958E.description: Determine what it means to be an American citizen and describe the achievements of famous and ordinary citizens.

A536E210DFE601314E3B68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the actions of heroes and heroines make a difference.

A5363BA0DFE601314E3968A86D17958E.description: Social Responsibility & Change - Students understand how social ideas and individual action lead to social, political, economic, and technological change.

A535E950DFE601314E3868A86D17958E.description: Explain how memorials help us to honor and remember people.

A5359490DFE601314E3768A86D17958E.description: Discuss how conflicts can be resolved through compromise.

A5350540DFE601314E3568A86D17958E.description: Nation Building and Development - Students understand the people, events, ideas, and conflicts that lead to the evolution of nations, empires, distinctive cultures, and political and economic ideas.

A534B4E0DFE601314E3468A86D17958E.description: Learn about individuals around the world and discuss their contributions.

A5341510DFE601314E3268A86D17958E.description: Using artifacts and primary sources, and investigate how individuals and families contributed to the founding and development of the local community.

A533D110DFE601314E3168A86D17958E.description: Learn about individuals in the community and discuss their contributions.

A5334130DFE601314E2F68A86D17958E.description: People, Cultures, and Civilizations - Students understand the development, characteristics, and interaction of people, cultures, societies, religion, and ideas.

A57478C0DFE601314E5868A86D17958E.description: Show responsibility for the well-being of oneself and family.

A5742810DFE601314E5768A86D17958E.description: Listen and participate as a member of a group in the classroom.

A5736BC0DFE601314E5568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an understanding of chronology by reading a timeline.

A5722A40DFE601314E5168A86D17958E.description: Present information orally and in writing.

A53D3880DFE601314E5068A86D17958E.description: Use the technology to effectively access information.

A53CF1C0DFE601314E4F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate positive social and ethical behaviors when using technology and discuss consequences of inappropriate use.

A53CA590DFE601314E4E68A86D17958E.description: Read maps, graphs, charts, and diagrams for information.

A53C5B50DFE601314E4D68A86D17958E.description: Use technology resources for problem solving, communication, and illustration of thoughts and ideas.

A53C14A0DFE601314E4C68A86D17958E.description: Conduct research by locating, gathering, and organizing information.

A53BC7D0DFE601314E4B68A86D17958E.description: Research a given social studies topic.

A53B10B0DFE601314E4968A86D17958E.description: Use content specific vocabulary in sentences.

A53A76C0DFE601314E4768A86D17958E.description: Identify main idea and sequence of events in a social studies context.

A53A30F0DFE601314E4668A86D17958E.description: Use pre-reading to skim text for main ideas.

A539E270DFE601314E4568A86D17958E.description: Use reading and writing to respond to literature.

document.title: Nevada Health Content Standards

A8C0B5D0DFE60131543768A86D17958E.description: Analyze how messages may influence community practices affecting the environment and consumer health.

A8C02060DFE60131543568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ways to influence and support others to make positive health choices.

A8BF6670DFE60131543368A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to support/promote family, personal, and community health.

A8BF0F40DFE60131543268A86D17958E.description: Analyze risky behaviors that may lead to the spread of communicable disease (i.e., sexually transmitted infections (STIs), hepatitis, mononucleosis, TB, flu)

A8BE8250DFE60131543068A86D17958E.description: Evaluate personal risk taking behavior (i.e., self-harming behaviors, harmful fads).

A8BE3F00DFE60131542F68A86D17958E.description: Understand basic safety, first aid, and lifesaving techniques (i.e, routine use of recreational safety equipment and procedures).

A8BDAD90DFE60131542D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate methods of response to risk taking behaviors including alcohol, tobacco and other drugs.

A8BCFBE0DFE60131542B68A86D17958E.description: Create a wellness plan that meets dietary guidelines and incorporates moderate to vigorous physical activity.

A8BC6840DFE60131542968A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of assuming responsibility for personal health behaviors.

A8BBE6D0DFE60131542768A86D17958E.description: (Self Management) Students will demonstrate the ability to practice health-enhancing behaviors and to avoid or reduce health risks.

A8BBA340DFE60131542668A86D17958E.description: Analyze how personal goals impact the community and environment.

A8BB14B0DFE60131542468A86D17958E.description: Analyze how personal health goals may need to be revised throughout your life.

A8BA8B50DFE60131542268A86D17958E.description: Apply time management strategies and skills needed to attain a personal long-term health goal.

A8B9F090DFE60131542068A86D17958E.description: (Goal Setting) Students will demonstrate the ability to use goal-setting skills to enhance health.

A8B9A6E0DFE60131541F68A86D17958E.description: Apply a decision-making process to a significant health issue or problem.

A8B8E5A0DFE60131541D68A86D17958E.description: Compare the short and long-term impact of health decisions.

A8B85B80DFE60131541B68A86D17958E.description: Compare the short and long-term impact of choices regarding substance use and abuse.

A8B7C7C0DFE60131541968A86D17958E.description: Defend healthy alternatives over unhealthy alternatives when making a decision.

A8B72E10DFE60131541768A86D17958E.description: (Decision Making) Students will demonstrate the ability to use decision-making skills to enhance health .

A8B6ECA0DFE60131541668A86D17958E.description: Implement refusal and negotiation skills necessary to resolve conflict.

A8B66790DFE60131541468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to ask for assistance to enhance the health of self and others.

A8B62150DFE60131541368A86D17958E.description: Practice appropriate methods of response to negative risk–taking situations including , alcohol, tobacco, and other drugs.

A8B57B10DFE60131541168A86D17958E.description: Express ways to communicate with others about perceived body image.

A8B4D9A0DFE60131540F68A86D17958E.description: Practice refusal and negotiation skills that avoid or reduce health risks.

A8B42A10DFE60131540D68A86D17958E.description: (Interpersonal Communication) Students will demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication skills to enhance health and to avoid or reduce health risks.

A8B3D5D0DFE60131540C68A86D17958E.description: Determine the accessibility of products and services that enhance health.

A8B34E10DFE60131540A68A86D17958E.description: Describe situations that may require professional health services.

A8B2C440DFE60131540868A86D17958E.description: (Accessing Information) Students will demonstrate the ability to access reliable health information, products, and services to enhance health.

A8B27AB0DFE60131540768A86D17958E.description: Critique a variety of consumer influences that affect health decisions.

A8B1E290DFE60131540568A86D17958E.description: Explain how local school and public health policies can influence health promotion and disease prevention.

A8B157D0DFE60131540368A86D17958E.description: Examine how individual family, peers, and information influence the personal use, misuse, and abuse of substances.

A8B0C410DFE60131540168A86D17958E.description: Examine how various sources influence your personal food choices.

A8B019C0DFE6013153FF68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the perceptions of norms influence healthy and risky behaviors.

A8AFCB40DFE6013153FE68A86D17958E.description: Explain how various sources affect individual health practices and behaviors.

A8AF3BA0DFE6013153FC68A86D17958E.description: (Analyze Influences) Students will analyze the influence of family, peers, culture, media, technology, and other factors on health behaviors.

A8AEEFE0DFE6013153FB68A86D17958E.description: Apply personal actions that contribute to the enhancement of the environment.

A8AE81F0DFE6013153FA68A86D17958E.description: Identify laws and regulations made to protect community health.

A8ADD0D0DFE6013153F868A86D17958E.description: Discuss how personal health behaviors can impact risk for illness/disease.

A8AD8D20DFE6013153F768A86D17958E.description: Describe how behaviors, pathogens, genetic history, and other factors are related to illness/disease prevention.

A8AD0590DFE6013153F568A86D17958E.description: Examine the likelihood of serious injury or illness if engaging in risky behaviors

A8ACB430DFE6013153F468A86D17958E.description: Develop a personal safety plan to reduce or prevent injuries.

A8AC3710DFE6013153F268A86D17958E.description: Analyze beneficial and harmful substance use.

A8ABB830DFE6013153F068A86D17958E.description: Describe how age, gender, physical activity, lifestyle, and heredity affect nutrient needs.

A8AB2F70DFE6013153EE68A86D17958E.description: Explain the interrelationships of emotional, intellectual, physical, and social health in adolescence.

A8AADE90DFE6013153ED68A86D17958E.description: Identify personal behaviors that affect the development and functioning of the body systems.

A8AA1E40DFE6013153EB68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between health behaviors and personal health.

A8A97F00DFE6013153E968A86D17958E.description: (Core Concepts) Students will comprehend concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention to enhance health.

document.title: Nevada Social Studies Standards

A59B4710DFE601314E7568A86D17958E.description: Identify their county, city, state, and country.

A59AB3C0DFE601314E7368A86D17958E.description: Global Relations - Students explain the different political systems in the world and how those systems relate to the United States and its citizens.

A59A6950DFE601314E7268A86D17958E.description: Identify sources of information people use to form an opinion.

A59A1D10DFE601314E7168A86D17958E.description: Define and give examples of state and local interest groups.

A59950A0DFE601314E6F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the qualities of a leader.

A598A800DFE601314E6D68A86D17958E.description: The Political Process - Students describe the roles of political parties, elections, interest groups, media, and public opinion in the democratic process.

A59804B0DFE601314E6B68A86D17958E.description: Name the three branches of state government.

document.title: Nevada Academic Content Standards for Mathematics

A9CC3CD0DFE6013155DB68A86D17958E.description: Solve real world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
comments: For example, how much chocolate will each person get if 3 people share 1/2 lb of chocolate equally? How many 1/3-cup servings are in 2 cups of raisins?

A9CBDC10DFE6013155DA68A86D17958E.description: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients.
comments: For example, create a story context for 4 ÷ (1/5), and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that 4 ÷ (1/5) = 20 because 20 × (1/5) = 4.

For example, create a story context for (1/3) ÷ 4, and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (1/3) ÷ 4 = 1/12 because (1/12) × 4 = 1/3.
A9CB8E70DFE6013155D968A86D17958E.description: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients.

A9CB2890DFE6013155D868A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.
comments: Students able to multiply fractions in general can develop strategies to divide fractions in general, by reasoning about the relationship between multiplication and division. But division of a fraction by a fraction is not a requirement at this grade

A9CAD720DFE6013155D768A86D17958E.description: Solve real world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

A9CA8E70DFE6013155D668A86D17958E.description: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number (recognizing multiplication by whole numbers greater than 1 as a familiar case); explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number; and relating the principle of fraction equivalence a/b = (n×a)/(n×b) to the effect of multiplying a/b by 1.

A9CA3FE0DFE6013155D568A86D17958E.description: Comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.

A9C9AF30DFE6013155D368A86D17958E.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles, and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.

A9C96CC0DFE6013155D268A86D17958E.description: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷ b.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to show (2/3) × 4 = 8/3, and create a story context for this equation. Do the same with (2/3) × (4/5) = 8/15. (In general, (a/b) × (c/d) = ac/bd.)

A9C92B10DFE6013155D168A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

A9C8E150DFE6013155D068A86D17958E.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.
comments: For example, interpret 3/4 as the result of dividing 3 by 4, noting that 3/4 multiplied by 4 equals 3, and that when 3 wholes are shared equally among 4 people each person has a share of size 3/4. If 9 people want to share a 50-pound sack of rice equally by weight, how many pounds of rice should each person get? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?

A9C89D70DFE6013155CF68A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.

comments: For example, recognize an incorrect result 2/5 + 1/2 = 3/7, by observing that 3/7 < 1/2.
A9C84FF0DFE6013155CE68A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole, including cases of unlike denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.

comments: For example, 2/3 + 5/4 = 8/12 + 15/12 = 23/12. (In general, a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd.)
A9C80770DFE6013155CD68A86D17958E.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators.

A9C7C670DFE6013155CC68A86D17958E.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.

comments: Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100

A9C73D90DFE6013155CA68A86D17958E.description: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

A9C6E200DFE6013155C968A86D17958E.description: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category.
comments: For example, all rectangles have four right angles and squares are rectangles, so all squares have four right angles.

A9C689E0DFE6013155C868A86D17958E.description: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.

A9C63A40DFE6013155C768A86D17958E.description: Represent real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

A9C5F230DFE6013155C668A86D17958E.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

A9C5A850DFE6013155C568A86D17958E.description: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

A9C4DE90DFE6013155C368A86D17958E.description: Recognize volume as additive. Find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

A9C49C80DFE6013155C268A86D17958E.description: Apply the formulas V = l × w × h and V = b × h for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems.

A9C45A10DFE6013155C168A86D17958E.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent threefold whole-number products as volumes, e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication.

A9C41780DFE6013155C068A86D17958E.description: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real world and mathematical problems involving volume.

A9C3D130DFE6013155BF68A86D17958E.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units.

A9C38450DFE6013155BE68A86D17958E.description: A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes is said to have a volume of n cubic units.

A9C31E40DFE6013155BD68A86D17958E.description: A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube," is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume, and can be used to measure volume.

A9C2D550DFE6013155BC68A86D17958E.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

A9C28F70DFE6013155BB68A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.

comments: For example, given different measurements of liquid in identical beakers, find the amount of liquid each beaker would contain if the total amount in all the beakers were redistributed equally.
A9C1AB40DFE6013155B868A86D17958E.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots.

A9C24A70DFE6013155BA68A86D17958E.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m), and use these conversions in solving multi-step, real world problems.

A9C20170DFE6013155B968A86D17958E.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

A9C0C530DFE6013155B568A86D17958E.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

A9C07F60DFE6013155B468A86D17958E.description: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

A9C03AF0DFE6013155B368A86D17958E.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

A9BFF150DFE6013155B268A86D17958E.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.

A9BF8A50DFE6013155B168A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

A9BF20B0DFE6013155B068A86D17958E.description: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

A9BEDBD0DFE6013155AF68A86D17958E.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form, e.g., 347.392 = 3 × 100 + 4 × 10 + 7 × 1 + 3 × (1/10) + 9 × (1/100) + 2 × (1/1000).

A9BE9A80DFE6013155AE68A86D17958E.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

A9BE5740DFE6013155AD68A86D17958E.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10, and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.

A9BE13C0DFE6013155AC68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

A9BD7E50DFE6013155AA68A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.

A9BD3750DFE6013155A968A86D17958E.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.
comments: For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 0, and given the rule "Add 6" and the starting number 0, generate terms in the resulting sequences, and observe that the terms in one sequence are twice the corresponding terms in the other sequence. Explain informally why this is so.

For example, express the calculation "add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2" as 2 × (8 + 7). Recognize that 3 × (18932 + 921) is three times as large as 18932 + 921, without having to calculate the indicated sum or product.
A9BC9910DFE6013155A768A86D17958E.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.

A9BC4520DFE6013155A668A86D17958E.description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
A9BB5EA0DFE6013155A368A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

A9BB1080DFE6013155A268A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

A9B9AD20DFE60131559E68A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

A9B8F8E0DFE60131559C68A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: Nevada Academic Content Standards for Mathematics

A9582D20DFE60131551A68A86D17958E.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

A957E3D0DFE60131551968A86D17958E.description: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.

A9579FA0DFE60131551868A86D17958E.description: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.
comments: Sizes are compared directly or visually, not compared by measuring.

A9575BC0DFE60131551768A86D17958E.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

A9532EF0DFE60131550968A86D17958E.description: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph.

A9567F70DFE60131551468A86D17958E.description: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.

A955DB70DFE60131551268A86D17958E.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2, …, and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.

A95589C0DFE60131551168A86D17958E.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

A9554970DFE60131551068A86D17958E.description: Relate addition and subtraction to length.

A953B420DFE60131550B68A86D17958E.description: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.

document.title: Nevada Academic Content Standards for English Language Arts

AD9AAF40DFE601315CAA68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal contrast, addition, and other logical relationships (e.g., however, although, nevertheless, similarly, moreover, in addition).

AD9A5C90DFE601315CA968A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonyms, antonyms, homographs) to better understand each of the words.

AD99FE90DFE601315CA868A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

AD999A10DFE601315CA768A86D17958E.description: Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors, in context.

AD993780DFE601315CA668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

AD98E940DFE601315CA568A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

AD98A100DFE601315CA468A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., photograph, photosynthesis).

AD985200DFE601315CA368A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., cause/effect relationships and comparisons in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

AD97FE30DFE601315CA268A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 5 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

AD976E80DFE601315CA068A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the varieties of English (e.g., dialects, registers) used in stories, dramas, or poems.

AD972440DFE601315C9F68A86D17958E.description: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

document.title: Nevada Academic Content Standards for Science

7E8EEA0A847D415F8741760D3BF62F94.description: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.

8DF2AA1BE682455488EE4B633F6B0A6A.description: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.

B8766B9A2C934350AF50C47D260A124A.description: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or a want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time, or cost.

5DCECFD33362403B85AF18321FE1B549.description: Obtain and combine information about ways individual communities use science ideas to protect the Earth's resources and environment.

3683BBDEB8B545B5836FB180542BB268.description: Describe and graph the amounts and percentages of water and fresh water in various reservoirs to provide evidence about the distribution of water on Earth.
comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to oceans, lakes, rivers, glaciers, ground water, and polar ice caps, and does not include the atmosphere.

DC9D1BAAD3614836A57A64DFD327553D.description: Develop a model using an example to describe ways the geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere, and/or atmosphere interact.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples could include the influence of the ocean on ecosystems, landform shape, and climate; the influence of the atmosphere on landforms and ecosystems through weather and climate; and the influence of mountain ranges on winds and clouds in the atmosphere. The geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere are each a system.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to the interactions of two systems at a time.

BAF60FF848434A64867515D1D181CA3E.description: Represent data in graphical displays to reveal patterns of daily changes in length and direction of shadows, day and night, and the seasonal appearance of some stars in the night sky.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of patterns could include the position and motion of Earth with respect to the sun and selected stars that are visible only in particular months.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include causes of seasons.

C876AF4A2532491D8D32FB5F03906B4E.description: Support an argument that differences in the apparent brightness of the sun compared to other stars is due to their relative distances from Earth.
comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to relative distances, not sizes, of stars. Assessment does not include other factors that affect apparent brightness (such as stellar masses, age, stage).

4BFD5EC14120439BADAF2CDE8BB699EF.description: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment.
comments: Clarifcation Statement: Emphasis is on the idea that matter that is not food (air, water, decomposed materials in soil) is changed by plants into matter that is food. Examples of systems could include organisms, ecosystems, and the Earth.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include molecular explanations.
Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the idea that plant matter comes mostly from air and water, not from the soil.
2C9AD401993E4B3B98BB4AB0ACEF4F52.description: Support an argument that plants get the materials they need for growth chiefly from air and water.

49FDBAE01E604932B8ED809C5F652729.description: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

7C9FD1E00F6D43158ECB101A3F8D99E8.description: Use models to describe that energy in animals' food (used for body repair, growth, motion, and to maintain body warmth) was once energy from the sun.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of models could include diagrams, and flow charts.

3B5DA9D3641946D8B79B9EBC6FACC2AF.description: Support an argument that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed down.
comments: Clarification Statement: "Down" is a local description of the direction that points toward the center of the spherical Earth.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include mathematical representation of gravitational force.

1EB9CBC6A7AB4E7CA57B3F2C9FBFD9F0.description: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

9CE468F0D31F48A79107444DB30D3CC2.description: Conduct an investigation to determine whether the mixing of two or more substances results in new substances.

comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of materials to be identified could include baking soda and other powders, metals, minerals, and liquids. Examples of properties could include color, hardness, reflectivity, electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, response to magnetic forces, and solubility; density is not intended as an identifiable property.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include density or distinguishing mass and weight.
E429F9B607FC4F51AC252F382E14AB37.description: Make observations and measurements to identify materials based on their properties.

AAB17DE3DEA24199BBF38005B68C6778.description: Measure and graph quantities to provide evidence that regardless of the type of change that occurs when heating, cooling, or mixing substances, the total weight of matter is conserved.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of reactions or changes could include phase changes, dissolving, and mixing that form new substances.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include distinguishing mass and weight.

C6B9AB5AFC2348FDACE648047BEDBE37.description: Develop a model to describe that matter is made of particles too small to be seen.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of evidence could include adding air to expand a basketball, compressing air in a syringe, dissolving sugar in water, and evaporating salt water.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include the atomic-scale mechanism of evaporation and condensation or defining the unseen particles.

document.title: Nevada Academic Content Standards for English Language Arts

AF510190DFE601315FE268A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

AF50A690DFE601315FE168A86D17958E.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

AF504940DFE601315FE068A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., euphemism, oxymoron) in context and analyze their role in the text.

AF4FD8C0DFE601315FDF68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

AF4F8020DFE601315FDE68A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

AF4F2CB0DFE601315FDD68A86D17958E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, or its etymology.

AF4EDEB0DFE601315FDC68A86D17958E.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., analyze, analysis, analytical; advocate, advocacy).

AF4E8E60DFE601315FDB68A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

AF4E2F60DFE601315FDA68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grades 9—10 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

AF4D9320DFE601315FD868A86D17958E.description: Write and edit work so that it conforms to the guidelines in a style manual (e.g., MLA Handbook, Turabian's Manual for Writers) appropriate for the discipline and writing type.

AF4D4450DFE601315FD768A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

AF4C3940DFE601315FD468A86D17958E.description: Use a colon to introduce a list or quotation.

AF4BE6B0DFE601315FD368A86D17958E.description: Use a semicolon (and perhaps a conjunctive adverb) to link two or more closely related independent clauses.

AF4B8610DFE601315FD268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

AF4B2840DFE601315FD168A86D17958E.description: Use various types of phrases (noun, verb, adjectival, adverbial, participial, prepositional, absolute) and clauses (independent, dependent; noun, relative, adverbial) to convey specific meanings and add variety and interest to writing or presentations.

AF4A76A0DFE601315FCF68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

AF48C880DFE601315FCB68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

AF4873F0DFE601315FCA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

AF4819E0DFE601315FC968A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

AF473C50DFE601315FC768A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

AF468C80DFE601315FC568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

AF462F60DFE601315FC468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

AF458510DFE601315FC268A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

AF452320DFE601315FC168A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

AF44CD30DFE601315FC068A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

AF447160DFE601315FBF68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence clearly, concisely, and logically such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and task.

AF43A2A0DFE601315FBD68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, identifying any fallacious reasoning or exaggerated or distorted evidence.

AF434BC0DFE601315FBC68A86D17958E.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source.

AF42FAB0DFE601315FBB68A86D17958E.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives, summarize points of agreement and disagreement, and, when warranted, qualify or justify their own views and understanding and make new connections in light of the evidence and reasoning presented.

AF42AA00DFE601315FBA68A86D17958E.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that relate the current discussion to broader themes or larger ideas; actively incorporate others into the discussion; and clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions.

AF4258A0DFE601315FB968A86D17958E.description: Work with peers to set rules for collegial discussions and decision-making (e.g., informal consensus, taking votes on key issues, presentation of alternate views), clear goals and deadlines, and individual roles as needed.

AF4204D0DFE601315FB868A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

AF4199D0DFE601315FB768A86D17958E.description: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grades 9—10 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

AF409350DFE601315FB468A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

AF4042B0DFE601315FB368A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

AF3FE300DFE601315FB268A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

AF3F47F0DFE601315FB068A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

B16ED73A983C4E909A8CA0FC8DD5C8B1.description: Analyze data from tests of two objects designed to solve the same problem to compare the strengths and weaknesses of how each performs.

DB8CB4FE12674F8EAB2853D10FE7968C.description: Obtain information to identify where water is found on Earth and that it can be solid or liquid.

comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include quantitative scaling in models.
26E085538F0C44ADAF398DEDB62C98AD.description: Develop a model to represent the shapes and kinds of land and bodies of water in an area.

072360D64DB947248ED82DEA464B8709.description: Compare multiple solutions designed to slow or prevent wind or water from changing the shape of the land.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of solutions could include different designs of dikes and windbreaks to hold back wind and water, and different designs for using shrubs, grass, and trees to hold back the land.

DE3B32A0B72A4C70818517FD88B3DEE7.description: Use information from several sources to provide evidence that Earth events can occur quickly or slowly.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of events and timescales could include volcanic explosions and earthquakes, which happen quickly and erosion of rocks, which occurs slowly.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include quantitative measurements of timescales.

854C12D0376D4FF8AF142696505B95C4.description: Make observations of plants and animals to compare the diversity of life in different habitats.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the diversity of living things in each of a variety of different habitats.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment does not include specific animal and plant names in specific habitats.

EDA8E59BB2DF4BCB971F8AA54ED7ACCF.description: Develop a simple model that mimics the function of an animal in dispersing seeds or pollinating plants.

comments: Assessment Boundary: Assessment is limited to testing one variable at a time.
2DBADF42CFE5469B8AEA90D36C0A469A.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to determine if plants need sunlight and water to grow.

comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of reversible changes could include materials such as water and butter at different temperatures. Examples of irreversible changes could include cooking an egg, freezing a plant leaf, and heating paper.
CE60535855B943F1ACF640E4A500FD0E.description: Construct an argument with evidence that some changes caused by heating or cooling can be reversed and some cannot.

comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of pieces could include blocks, building bricks, or other assorted small objects.
99F5A9C81F4C47F58109B78C0E69CD5A.description: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account of how an object made of a small set of pieces can be disassembled and made into a new object.

120F1A2A015847289F08440B8B200637.description: Analyze data obtained from testing different materials to determine which materials have the properties that are best suited for an intended purpose.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of properties could include, strength, flexibility, hardness, texture, and absorbency.
Assessment Boundary: Assessment of quantitative measurements is limited to length.

CE30FA9CC1E04C4D8E006CE746EED1BA.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to describe and classify different kinds of materials by their observable properties.
comments: Clarification Statement: Observations could include color, texture, hardness, and flexibility. Patterns could include the similar properties that different materials share.
